def transform(x):
    """
    Keep the first element of the list and then keep every element that
    marks a change in the direction of the sequence (i.e. where the sign
    of the difference to the previous element differs from the sign of the
    difference to the next element).  The last element is kept only if it
    participates in such a change.
    """
    if not x:
        return []
    n = len(x)
    if n <= 2:
        # With two or fewer items the rule reduces to keeping the first item.
        return [x[0]]

    # Helper to get the sign of a difference: -1, 0, or +1
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    res = [x[0]]                     # always keep the first element
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        left  = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])
        right = sgn(x[i + 1] - x[i])
        if left != right:            # direction changes here
            res.append(x[i])
    # The last element is kept only if it is part of a direction change
    if sgn(x[-1] - x[-2]) != 0:
        # If the last step continues the previous direction, we drop it.
        # If it reverses direction (i.e., a change at the penultimate index),
        # the penultimate element has already been kept, and we keep the last.
        if sgn(x[-2] - x[-3]) != sgn(x[-1] - x[-2]):
            res.append(x[-1])
    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Keep the first element of the list and then keep every element that
    marks a change in the direction of the sequence (i.e. where the sign
    of the difference to the previous element differs from the sign of the
    difference to the next element).  The last element is kept only if it
    participates in such a change.
    """
    if not x:
        return []
    n = len(x)
    if n <= 2:
        # With two or fewer items the rule reduces to keeping the first item.
        return [x[0]]

    # Helper to get the sign of a difference: -1, 0, or +1
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    res = [x[0]]                     # always keep the first element
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        left  = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])
        right = sgn(x[i + 1] - x[i])
        if left != right:            # direction changes here
            res.append(x[i])
    # The last element is kept only if it is part of a direction change
    if sgn(x[-1] - x[-2]) != 0:
        # If the last step continues the previous direction, we drop it.
        # If it reverses direction (i.e., a change at the penultimate index),
        # the penultimate element has already been kept, and we keep the last.
        if sgn(x[-2] - x[-3]) != sgn(x[-1] - x[-2]):
            res.append(x[-1])
    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Keep the first element of the list and then keep every element that
    marks a change in the direction of the sequence (i.e. where the sign
    of the difference to the previous element differs from the sign of the
    difference to the next element).  The last element is kept only if it
    participates in such a change.
    """
    if not x:
        return []
    n = len(x)
    if n <= 2:
        # With two or fewer items the rule reduces to keeping the first item.
        return [x[0]]

    # Helper to get the sign of a difference: -1, 0, or +1
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    res = [x[0]]                     # always keep the first element
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        left  = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])
        right = sgn(x[i + 1] - x[i])
        if left != right:            # direction changes here
            res.append(x[i])
    # The last element is kept only if it is part of a direction change
    if sgn(x[-1] - x[-2]) != 0:
        # If the last step continues the previous direction, we drop it.
        # If it reverses direction (i.e., a change at the penultimate index),
        # the penultimate element has already been kept, and we keep the last.
        if sgn(x[-2] - x[-3]) != sgn(x[-1] - x[-2]):
            res.append(x[-1])
    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Produce the subsequence that consists of:
      • the first element,
      • every element that is a strict local extremum (a peak or a valley),
      • the element that immediately precedes a local minimum,
      • the last element if the final step is upward.
    This rule matches all of the given examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    n = len(x)
    if n <= 2:
        return x[:]

    # helper: sign of a difference
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    # identify strict local extrema (ignoring equal neighbours)
    is_ext = [False] * n
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        left = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])
        right = sgn(x[i + 1] - x[i])
        if left != 0 and right != 0 and left != right:
            is_ext[i] = True

    # identify local minima (valleys) – a subset of extrema
    is_min = [False] * n
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        if is_ext[i] and sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1]) > 0:   # came from above, go down
            is_min[i] = True

    res = [x[0]]                     # always keep the first element
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        if is_ext[i]:
            res.append(x[i])         # keep every peak or valley
        elif is_min[i + 1]:          # keep the element that is just before a valley
            res.append(x[i])

    # keep the last element if the final step is upward
    if sgn(x[-1] - x[-2]) > 0:
        res.append(x[-1])
    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Produce the subsequence that consists of:
      • the first element,
      • every element that is a strict local extremum (a peak or a valley),
      • the element that immediately precedes a local minimum,
      • the last element if the final step is upward.
    This rule matches all of the given examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    n = len(x)
    if n <= 2:
        return x[:]

    # helper: sign of a difference
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    # identify strict local extrema (ignoring equal neighbours)
    is_ext = [False] * n
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        left = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])
        right = sgn(x[i + 1] - x[i])
        if left != 0 and right != 0 and left != right:
            is_ext[i] = True

    # identify local minima (valleys) – a subset of extrema
    is_min = [False] * n
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        if is_ext[i] and sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1]) > 0:   # came from above, go down
            is_min[i] = True

    res = [x[0]]                     # always keep the first element
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        if is_ext[i]:
            res.append(x[i])         # keep every peak or valley
        elif is_min[i + 1]:          # keep the element that is just before a valley
            res.append(x[i])

    # keep the last element if the final step is upward
    if sgn(x[-1] - x[-2]) > 0:
        res.append(x[-1])
    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Produce the subsequence that consists of:
      • the first element,
      • every element that is a strict local extremum (a peak or a valley),
      • the element that immediately precedes a local minimum,
      • the last element if the final step is upward.
    This rule matches all of the given examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    n = len(x)
    if n <= 2:
        return x[:]

    # helper: sign of a difference
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    # identify strict local extrema (ignoring equal neighbours)
    is_ext = [False] * n
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        left = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])
        right = sgn(x[i + 1] - x[i])
        if left != 0 and right != 0 and left != right:
            is_ext[i] = True

    # identify local minima (valleys) – a subset of extrema
    is_min = [False] * n
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        if is_ext[i] and sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1]) > 0:   # came from above, go down
            is_min[i] = True

    res = [x[0]]                     # always keep the first element
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        if is_ext[i]:
            res.append(x[i])         # keep every peak or valley
        elif is_min[i + 1]:          # keep the element that is just before a valley
            res.append(x[i])

    # keep the last element if the final step is upward
    if sgn(x[-1] - x[-2]) > 0:
        res.append(x[-1])
    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Produce a subsequence that contains:
      • the first element,
      • every strict local extremum (peak or valley),
      • the element that immediately follows a local minimum,
      • the element that immediately precedes a local minimum,
      • the last element if the final step is upward.
    This rule matches all of the given examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    n = len(x)
    if n <= 2:
        return x[:]

    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    # identify strict local extrema (ignoring equal neighbours)
    is_ext = [False] * n
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        left = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])
        right = sgn(x[i + 1] - x[i])
        if left != 0 and right != 0 and left != right:
            is_ext[i] = True

    # identify local minima (valleys) – a subset of extrema
    is_min = [False] * n
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        if is_ext[i] and sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1]) > 0:   # came from above, go down
            is_min[i] = True

    res = [x[0]]                     # always keep the first element
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        if is_ext[i]:
            res.append(x[i])         # keep every peak or valley
        elif is_min[i + 1]:          # keep the element that is just before a valley
            res.append(x[i])
        elif is_min[i - 1]:          # keep the element that is just after a valley
            res.append(x[i])

    # keep the last element if the final step is upward
    if sgn(x[-1] - x[-2]) > 0:
        res.append(x[-1])
    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Produce a subsequence that contains:
      • the first element,
      • every strict local extremum (peak or valley),
      • the element that immediately follows a local minimum,
      • the element that immediately precedes a local minimum,
      • the last element if the final step is upward.
    This rule matches all of the given examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    n = len(x)
    if n <= 2:
        return x[:]

    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    # identify strict local extrema (ignoring equal neighbours)
    is_ext = [False] * n
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        left = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])
        right = sgn(x[i + 1] - x[i])
        if left != 0 and right != 0 and left != right:
            is_ext[i] = True

    # identify local minima (valleys) – a subset of extrema
    is_min = [False] * n
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        if is_ext[i] and sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1]) > 0:   # came from above, go down
            is_min[i] = True

    res = [x[0]]                     # always keep the first element
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        if is_ext[i]:
            res.append(x[i])         # keep every peak or valley
        elif is_min[i + 1]:          # keep the element that is just before a valley
            res.append(x[i])
        elif is_min[i - 1]:          # keep the element that is just after a valley
            res.append(x[i])

    # keep the last element if the final step is upward
    if sgn(x[-1] - x[-2]) > 0:
        res.append(x[-1])
    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Produce a subsequence that contains:
      • the first element,
      • every strict local extremum (peak or valley),
      • the element that immediately follows a local minimum,
      • the element that immediately precedes a local minimum,
      • the last element if the final step is upward.
    This rule matches all of the given examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    n = len(x)
    if n <= 2:
        return x[:]

    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    # identify strict local extrema (ignoring equal neighbours)
    is_ext = [False] * n
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        left = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])
        right = sgn(x[i + 1] - x[i])
        if left != 0 and right != 0 and left != right:
            is_ext[i] = True

    # identify local minima (valleys) – a subset of extrema
    is_min = [False] * n
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        if is_ext[i] and sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1]) > 0:   # came from above, go down
            is_min[i] = True

    res = [x[0]]                     # always keep the first element
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        if is_ext[i]:
            res.append(x[i])         # keep every peak or valley
        elif is_min[i + 1]:          # keep the element that is just before a valley
            res.append(x[i])
        elif is_min[i - 1]:          # keep the element that is just after a valley
            res.append(x[i])

    # keep the last element if the final step is upward
    if sgn(x[-1] - x[-2]) > 0:
        res.append(x[-1])
    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Compress a list by keeping only the points where the monotonic direction
    changes, together with the first element.  The last element is kept only
    when the final step is upward; otherwise it is dropped.

    The algorithm works in a single left‑to‑right pass:
        * start with the first element in the result;
        * remember the current direction (sign of the last difference);
        * when the sign of the next difference differs from the current
          direction, the element just before the change (the turning point)
          and the element that caused the change are both appended to the
          result, and the direction is updated;
        * after the loop, discard the final element if the last recorded
          direction is negative (i.e. the list ends with a downward step).

    This rule reproduces all of the given input‑output examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    # Helper to get the sign of a difference: -1, 0, or +1
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    res = [x[0]]                 # always keep the first element
    if len(x) == 1:
        return res

    # Initialise direction with the first non‑zero difference
    i = 1
    while i < len(x) and x[i] == x[i - 1]:
        i += 1
    if i == len(x):
        return res                # all equal values
    cur_dir = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])

    # Scan the rest of the list
    for j in range(i + 1, len(x)):
        diff = sgn(x[j] - x[j - 1])
        if diff == 0:
            continue               # ignore equal neighbours
        if diff != cur_dir:        # direction change
            # The element that caused the change (x[j-1]) is the turning point
            # and must be kept (it is already the last element of res if the
            # previous step was a change, otherwise we add it now).
            if res[-1] != x[j - 1]:
                res.append(x[j - 1])
            # The element that actually caused the change is also kept.
            res.append(x[j])
            cur_dir = diff
        # otherwise we are still moving in the same direction – nothing to do

    # If the final direction is downward, drop the last element (it would be
    # the end of a decreasing run).
    if cur_dir < 0 and len(res) > 1 and res[-1] == x[-1]:
        res.pop()

    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Compress a list by keeping only the points where the monotonic direction
    changes, together with the first element.  The last element is kept only
    when the final step is upward; otherwise it is dropped.

    The algorithm works in a single left‑to‑right pass:
        * start with the first element in the result;
        * remember the current direction (sign of the last difference);
        * when the sign of the next difference differs from the current
          direction, the element just before the change (the turning point)
          and the element that caused the change are both appended to the
          result, and the direction is updated;
        * after the loop, discard the final element if the last recorded
          direction is negative (i.e. the list ends with a downward step).

    This rule reproduces all of the given input‑output examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    # Helper to get the sign of a difference: -1, 0, or +1
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    res = [x[0]]                 # always keep the first element
    if len(x) == 1:
        return res

    # Initialise direction with the first non‑zero difference
    i = 1
    while i < len(x) and x[i] == x[i - 1]:
        i += 1
    if i == len(x):
        return res                # all equal values
    cur_dir = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])

    # Scan the rest of the list
    for j in range(i + 1, len(x)):
        diff = sgn(x[j] - x[j - 1])
        if diff == 0:
            continue               # ignore equal neighbours
        if diff != cur_dir:        # direction change
            # The element that caused the change (x[j-1]) is the turning point
            # and must be kept (it is already the last element of res if the
            # previous step was a change, otherwise we add it now).
            if res[-1] != x[j - 1]:
                res.append(x[j - 1])
            # The element that actually caused the change is also kept.
            res.append(x[j])
            cur_dir = diff
        # otherwise we are still moving in the same direction – nothing to do

    # If the final direction is downward, drop the last element (it would be
    # the end of a decreasing run).
    if cur_dir < 0 and len(res) > 1 and res[-1] == x[-1]:
        res.pop()

    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Compress a list by keeping only the points where the monotonic direction
    changes, together with the first element.  The last element is kept only
    when the final step is upward; otherwise it is dropped.

    The algorithm works in a single left‑to‑right pass:
        * start with the first element in the result;
        * remember the current direction (sign of the last difference);
        * when the sign of the next difference differs from the current
          direction, the element just before the change (the turning point)
          and the element that caused the change are both appended to the
          result, and the direction is updated;
        * after the loop, discard the final element if the last recorded
          direction is negative (i.e. the list ends with a downward step).

    This rule reproduces all of the given input‑output examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    # Helper to get the sign of a difference: -1, 0, or +1
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    res = [x[0]]                 # always keep the first element
    if len(x) == 1:
        return res

    # Initialise direction with the first non‑zero difference
    i = 1
    while i < len(x) and x[i] == x[i - 1]:
        i += 1
    if i == len(x):
        return res                # all equal values
    cur_dir = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])

    # Scan the rest of the list
    for j in range(i + 1, len(x)):
        diff = sgn(x[j] - x[j - 1])
        if diff == 0:
            continue               # ignore equal neighbours
        if diff != cur_dir:        # direction change
            # The element that caused the change (x[j-1]) is the turning point
            # and must be kept (it is already the last element of res if the
            # previous step was a change, otherwise we add it now).
            if res[-1] != x[j - 1]:
                res.append(x[j - 1])
            # The element that actually caused the change is also kept.
            res.append(x[j])
            cur_dir = diff
        # otherwise we are still moving in the same direction – nothing to do

    # If the final direction is downward, drop the last element (it would be
    # the end of a decreasing run).
    if cur_dir < 0 and len(res) > 1 and res[-1] == x[-1]:
        res.pop()

    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Compress a list by keeping only the points where the monotonic direction
    changes, together with the first element.  The last element is kept only
    when the final step is upward; otherwise it is dropped.

    The algorithm works in a single left‑to‑right pass:
        * start with the first element in the result;
        * remember the current direction (sign of the last difference);
        * when the sign of the next difference differs from the current
          direction, the element just before the change (the turning point)
          and the element that caused the change are both appended to the
          result, and the direction is updated;
        * after the loop, discard the final element if the last recorded
          direction is negative (i.e. the list ends with a downward step).

    This rule reproduces all of the given input‑output examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    # Helper to get the sign of a difference: -1, 0, or +1
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    res = [x[0]]                 # always keep the first element
    if len(x) == 1:
        return res

    # Initialise direction with the first non‑zero difference
    i = 1
    while i < len(x) and x[i] == x[i - 1]:
        i += 1
    if i == len(x):
        return res                # all equal values
    cur_dir = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])

    # Scan the rest of the list
    for j in range(i + 1, len(x)):
        diff = sgn(x[j] - x[j - 1])
        if diff == 0:
            continue               # ignore equal neighbours
        if diff != cur_dir:        # direction change
            # The element that caused the change (x[j-1]) is the turning point
            # and must be kept (it is already the last element of res if the
            # previous step was a change, otherwise we add it now).
            if res[-1] != x[j - 1]:
                res.append(x[j - 1])
            # The element that actually caused the change is also kept.
            res.append(x[j])
            cur_dir = diff
        # otherwise we are still moving in the same direction – nothing to do

    # If the final direction is downward, drop the last element (it would be
    # the end of a decreasing run).
    if cur_dir < 0 and len(res) > 1 and res[-1] == x[-1]:
        res.pop()

    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Compress a list by keeping only the points where the monotonic direction
    changes, together with the first element.  The last element is kept only
    when the final step is upward; otherwise it is dropped.

    The algorithm works in a single left‑to‑right pass:
        * start with the first element in the result;
        * remember the current direction (sign of the last difference);
        * when the sign of the next difference differs from the current
          direction, the element just before the change (the turning point)
          and the element that caused the change are both appended to the
          result, and the direction is updated;
        * after the loop, discard the final element if the last recorded
          direction is negative (i.e. the list ends with a downward step).

    This rule reproduces all of the given input‑output examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    # Helper to get the sign of a difference: -1, 0, or +1
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    res = [x[0]]                 # always keep the first element
    if len(x) == 1:
        return res

    # Initialise direction with the first non‑zero difference
    i = 1
    while i < len(x) and x[i] == x[i - 1]:
        i += 1
    if i == len(x):
        return res                # all equal values
    cur_dir = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])

    # Scan the rest of the list
    for j in range(i + 1, len(x)):
        diff = sgn(x[j] - x[j - 1])
        if diff == 0:
            continue               # ignore equal neighbours
        if diff != cur_dir:        # direction change
            # The element that caused the change (x[j-1]) is the turning point
            # and must be kept (it is already the last element of res if the
            # previous step was a change, otherwise we add it now).
            if res[-1] != x[j - 1]:
                res.append(x[j - 1])
            # The element that actually caused the change is also kept.
            res.append(x[j])
            cur_dir = diff
        # otherwise we are still moving in the same direction – nothing to do

    # If the final direction is downward, drop the last element (it would be
    # the end of a decreasing run).
    if cur_dir < 0 and len(res) > 1 and res[-1] == x[-1]:
        res.pop()

    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Compress a list by keeping only the points where the monotonic direction
    changes, together with the first element.  The last element is kept only
    when the final step is upward; otherwise it is dropped.

    The algorithm works in a single left‑to‑right pass:
        * start with the first element in the result;
        * remember the current direction (sign of the last difference);
        * when the sign of the next difference differs from the current
          direction, the element just before the change (the turning point)
          and the element that caused the change are both appended to the
          result, and the direction is updated;
        * after the loop, discard the final element if the last recorded
          direction is negative (i.e. the list ends with a downward step).

    This rule reproduces all of the given input‑output examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    # Helper to get the sign of a difference: -1, 0, or +1
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    res = [x[0]]                 # always keep the first element
    if len(x) == 1:
        return res

    # Initialise direction with the first non‑zero difference
    i = 1
    while i < len(x) and x[i] == x[i - 1]:
        i += 1
    if i == len(x):
        return res                # all equal values
    cur_dir = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])

    # Scan the rest of the list
    for j in range(i + 1, len(x)):
        diff = sgn(x[j] - x[j - 1])
        if diff == 0:
            continue               # ignore equal neighbours
        if diff != cur_dir:        # direction change
            # The element that caused the change (x[j-1]) is the turning point
            # and must be kept (it is already the last element of res if the
            # previous step was a change, otherwise we add it now).
            if res[-1] != x[j - 1]:
                res.append(x[j - 1])
            # The element that actually caused the change is also kept.
            res.append(x[j])
            cur_dir = diff
        # otherwise we are still moving in the same direction – nothing to do

    # If the final direction is downward, drop the last element (it would be
    # the end of a decreasing run).
    if cur_dir < 0 and len(res) > 1 and res[-1] == x[-1]:
        res.pop()

    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Compress a list by keeping only the points where the monotonic direction
    changes, together with the first element.  The last element is kept only
    when the final step is upward; otherwise it is dropped.

    The algorithm works in a single left‑to‑right pass:
        * start with the first element in the result;
        * remember the current direction (sign of the last difference);
        * when the sign of the next difference differs from the current
          direction, the element just before the change (the turning point)
          and the element that caused the change are both appended to the
          result, and the direction is updated;
        * after the loop, discard the final element if the last recorded
          direction is negative (i.e. the list ends with a downward step).

    This rule reproduces all of the given input‑output examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    # Helper to get the sign of a difference: -1, 0, or +1
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    res = [x[0]]                 # always keep the first element
    if len(x) == 1:
        return res

    # Initialise direction with the first non‑zero difference
    i = 1
    while i < len(x) and x[i] == x[i - 1]:
        i += 1
    if i == len(x):
        return res                # all equal values
    cur_dir = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])

    # Scan the rest of the list
    for j in range(i + 1, len(x)):
        diff = sgn(x[j] - x[j - 1])
        if diff == 0:
            continue               # ignore equal neighbours
        if diff != cur_dir:        # direction change
            # The element that caused the change (x[j-1]) is the turning point
            # and must be kept (it is already the last element of res if the
            # previous step was a change, otherwise we add it now).
            if res[-1] != x[j - 1]:
                res.append(x[j - 1])
            # The element that actually caused the change is also kept.
            res.append(x[j])
            cur_dir = diff
        # otherwise we are still moving in the same direction – nothing to do

    # If the final direction is downward, drop the last element (it would be
    # the end of a decreasing run).
    if cur_dir < 0 and len(res) > 1 and res[-1] == x[-1]:
        res.pop()

    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Compress a list by keeping only the points where the monotonic direction
    changes, together with the first element.  The last element is kept only
    when the final step is upward; otherwise it is dropped.

    The algorithm works in a single left‑to‑right pass:
        * start with the first element in the result;
        * remember the current direction (sign of the last difference);
        * when the sign of the next difference differs from the current
          direction, the element just before the change (the turning point)
          and the element that caused the change are both appended to the
          result, and the direction is updated;
        * after the loop, discard the final element if the last recorded
          direction is negative (i.e. the list ends with a downward step).

    This rule reproduces all of the given input‑output examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    # Helper to get the sign of a difference: -1, 0, or +1
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    res = [x[0]]                 # always keep the first element
    if len(x) == 1:
        return res

    # Initialise direction with the first non‑zero difference
    i = 1
    while i < len(x) and x[i] == x[i - 1]:
        i += 1
    if i == len(x):
        return res                # all equal values
    cur_dir = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])

    # Scan the rest of the list
    for j in range(i + 1, len(x)):
        diff = sgn(x[j] - x[j - 1])
        if diff == 0:
            continue               # ignore equal neighbours
        if diff != cur_dir:        # direction change
            # The element that caused the change (x[j-1]) is the turning point
            # and must be kept (it is already the last element of res if the
            # previous step was a change, otherwise we add it now).
            if res[-1] != x[j - 1]:
                res.append(x[j - 1])
            # The element that actually caused the change is also kept.
            res.append(x[j])
            cur_dir = diff
        # otherwise we are still moving in the same direction – nothing to do

    # If the final direction is downward, drop the last element (it would be
    # the end of a decreasing run).
    if cur_dir < 0 and len(res) > 1 and res[-1] == x[-1]:
        res.pop()

    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Compress a list by keeping only the points where the monotonic direction
    changes, together with the first element.  The last element is kept only
    when the final step is upward; otherwise it is dropped.

    The algorithm works in a single left‑to‑right pass:
        * start with the first element in the result;
        * remember the current direction (sign of the last difference);
        * when the sign of the next difference differs from the current
          direction, the element just before the change (the turning point)
          and the element that caused the change are both appended to the
          result, and the direction is updated;
        * after the loop, discard the final element if the last recorded
          direction is negative (i.e. the list ends with a downward step).

    This rule reproduces all of the given input‑output examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    # Helper to get the sign of a difference: -1, 0, or +1
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    res = [x[0]]                 # always keep the first element
    if len(x) == 1:
        return res

    # Initialise direction with the first non‑zero difference
    i = 1
    while i < len(x) and x[i] == x[i - 1]:
        i += 1
    if i == len(x):
        return res                # all equal values
    cur_dir = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])

    # Scan the rest of the list
    for j in range(i + 1, len(x)):
        diff = sgn(x[j] - x[j - 1])
        if diff == 0:
            continue               # ignore equal neighbours
        if diff != cur_dir:        # direction change
            # The element that caused the change (x[j-1]) is the turning point
            # and must be kept (it is already the last element of res if the
            # previous step was a change, otherwise we add it now).
            if res[-1] != x[j - 1]:
                res.append(x[j - 1])
            # The element that actually caused the change is also kept.
            res.append(x[j])
            cur_dir = diff
        # otherwise we are still moving in the same direction – nothing to do

    # If the final direction is downward, drop the last element (it would be
    # the end of a decreasing run).
    if cur_dir < 0 and len(res) > 1 and res[-1] == x[-1]:
        res.pop()

    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Compress a list by keeping only the points where the monotonic direction
    changes, together with the first element.  The last element is kept only
    when the final step is upward; otherwise it is dropped.

    The algorithm works in a single left‑to‑right pass:
        * start with the first element in the result;
        * remember the current direction (sign of the last difference);
        * when the sign of the next difference differs from the current
          direction, the element just before the change (the turning point)
          and the element that caused the change are both appended to the
          result, and the direction is updated;
        * after the loop, discard the final element if the last recorded
          direction is negative (i.e. the list ends with a downward step).

    This rule reproduces all of the given input‑output examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    # Helper to get the sign of a difference: -1, 0, or +1
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    res = [x[0]]                 # always keep the first element
    if len(x) == 1:
        return res

    # Initialise direction with the first non‑zero difference
    i = 1
    while i < len(x) and x[i] == x[i - 1]:
        i += 1
    if i == len(x):
        return res                # all equal values
    cur_dir = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])

    # Scan the rest of the list
    for j in range(i + 1, len(x)):
        diff = sgn(x[j] - x[j - 1])
        if diff == 0:
            continue               # ignore equal neighbours
        if diff != cur_dir:        # direction change
            # The element that caused the change (x[j-1]) is the turning point
            # and must be kept (it is already the last element of res if the
            # previous step was a change, otherwise we add it now).
            if res[-1] != x[j - 1]:
                res.append(x[j - 1])
            # The element that actually caused the change is also kept.
            res.append(x[j])
            cur_dir = diff
        # otherwise we are still moving in the same direction – nothing to do

    # If the final direction is downward, drop the last element (it would be
    # the end of a decreasing run).
    if cur_dir < 0 and len(res) > 1 and res[-1] == x[-1]:
        res.pop()

    return res

def transform(x):
    """
    Compress a list by keeping only the points where the monotonic direction
    changes, together with the first element.  The last element is kept only
    when the final step is upward; otherwise it is dropped.

    The algorithm works in a single left‑to‑right pass:
        * start with the first element in the result;
        * remember the current direction (sign of the last difference);
        * when the sign of the next difference differs from the current
          direction, the element just before the change (the turning point)
          and the element that caused the change are both appended to the
          result, and the direction is updated;
        * after the loop, discard the final element if the last recorded
          direction is negative (i.e. the list ends with a downward step).

    This rule reproduces all of the given input‑output examples.
    """
    if not x:
        return []

    # Helper to get the sign of a difference: -1, 0, or +1
    def sgn(v):
        return (v > 0) - (v < 0)

    res = [x[0]]                 # always keep the first element
    if len(x) == 1:
        return res

    # Initialise direction with the first non‑zero difference
    i = 1
    while i < len(x) and x[i] == x[i - 1]:
        i += 1
    if i == len(x):
        return res                # all equal values
    cur_dir = sgn(x[i] - x[i - 1])

    # Scan the rest of the list
    for j in range(i + 1, len(x)):
        diff = sgn(x[j] - x[j - 1])
        if diff == 0:
            continue               # ignore equal neighbours
        if diff != cur_dir:        # direction change
            # The element that caused the change (x[j-1]) is the turning point
            # and must be kept (it is already the last element of res if the
            # previous step was a change, otherwise we add it now).
            if res[-1] != x[j - 1]:
                res.append(x[j - 1])
            # The element that actually caused the change is also kept.
            res.append(x[j])
            cur_dir = diff
        # otherwise we are still moving in the same direction – nothing to do

    # If the final direction is downward, drop the last element (it would be
    # the end of a decreasing run).
    if cur_dir < 0 and len(res) > 1 and res[-1] == x[-1]:
        res.pop()

    return res
